If Trump wins the GOP nomination, members of the RNC will sulk and pout and secretly (and perhaps in some cases not so secretly) hope that Hillary wins the election.

The GOP can defeat Trump at the last moment, regardless of what we the people think about it, To understand how, you have to understand how many delegates each state offers, the types of delegates involved and how the states allocate them. There are 2472 total delegates and Trump need 1237 (half the total + 1) to win the nomination.

First, you have the states delegates, each state gets 10 at large delegates, + an additional 3 for each congressional district. I am not doing the math for all the states, but my state has 36 congressional Districts, so that is 108 delegates + the 10, for a total of 128 delegates.

Second, you have the type of state, Some are winner-takes-all and others states are proportional, with a bonus chunk awarded to the candidate that wins the most votes in that state. Again, I am not going through all the states, but mine is proportional.

The point being, if Trump wins the winner takes all and the bonus delegates for winning the plurality in proportional states, that gives him about 500 delegates. To win the nomination, you need 1237, so he is still about 737 delegates shy, he would need to make these up through bonus delegates, which are extras assigned to traditionally blue states and super-delegates, which are unpledged delegates whose votes to not have to reflect their region or state they represent.

This is where a brokered convention becomes tricky, because it clearly does not represent what your base wants, and tantamount to political suicide. The last nominee (nominee, not president) that was produced by a brokered convention was in FDR in 1932.
